question: Under the baked-in step skeleton (Register + N authored work steps + verification/full-suite/close-out), how many authored WORK steps N may a session declare? The 5-step cap measured by Set 111 S4 was taken on specs whose 5 declared steps already absorbed the ceremony, so it cannot be carried over unexamined: historical '5 declared' meant roughly 3-4 real work steps, while '4 + N' declared now contains only N.
decision: N = 3 authored work steps, so 7 declared steps per session (authoring.max_steps_per_session = 7). 3 is the value that holds the Set 111 S4 measured 42-minute median once the ceremony is subtracted. The operator's opening suggestion of N = 4 was put to the operator alongside it and REJECTED at ratification: it is a deliberate loosening rather than a re-count, and sessionSizeException already exists for genuine overruns.

options.consequence: Holds the measured 42-minute median: Set 111 S4 found 1-5 declared steps ran a 42-min median / 110-min p90 / 10% over two hours, and those specs spent about two of their declared steps on ceremony, so 3 real work steps is the middle of the measured band rather than its edge. Costs authors a split, or a declared sessionSizeException, on the fourth work step. Reversible: the cap is one integer in router-config.yaml.

options.option: N = 4 authored work steps (8 declared) - the operator's opening suggestion.
options.consequence: A deliberate loosening past the measured band. Set 111 S4's 6-8 declared band ran an 84-minute median with a 386-minute p90 and 28% of sessions past two hours; while those 8 declared steps were more work-dense than 4+4 would be, nothing in the measurement supports 4 work steps, so it would arrive as an artifact of re-counting rather than as evidence. Also reversible, but it sets the looser number as the baseline everyone anchors on.

Silently loosens the real budget from 3-4 work steps to 5 while appearing to change nothing, because the same integer now counts four ceremony steps it did not count before. This is the failure the re-baselining exists to prevent.

operator_attestation: Operator ratified N = 3 on 2026-08-12 at the Session 1 registration stop, from an education-mode brief that named N = 4 as their own opening suggestion and the Set 111 S4 measurement as the evidence. Recorded because the source-of-record note marks the question 'Unresolved - the operator skipped the question'.

question: The step-shape check lands against a corpus of 45 specs / 363 planned sessions of which exactly 3 conform - and all 3 are this set's own. Does the check BLOCK the existing non-conforming corpus, report it, or apply only to new sets?
decision: Blocking for sets that have not started; an informational note for every set that has already started, completed, or was cancelled. A set is 'not started' when it has no session-state.json or its status is not-started - the same file the repo already treats as the single source of truth for set progress. The blocking verdict is named 'requires restructuring', never 'refused'. Per the operator, the note on already-started sets is explicitly NOT a warning: those specs were authored under a different approach at a different time, and nothing about them is wrong.

options.option: Requires-restructuring (blocking) for unstarted sets; informational note for started/complete/cancelled sets.
options.consequence: Bites on day one - 113, 118, 121 and 122 are unstarted and non-conforming, so the check has something it genuinely fails, and a brand-new spec with no state file at all is the primary authoring-time path. The restructuring cost lands only where it is cheapest (an unstarted spec is a text edit, and 118's is already scheduled for Session 3). Costs one read of session-state.json inside a previously pure-text checker. Reversible: the gating predicate is one function.

options.option: Advisory everywhere - the check reports the shape but never fails.
options.consequence: Nothing can fail it on day one, which is exactly the shape L-112-1 warns about: a gate that only ever passes is indistinguishable from one that checks nothing. It would also leave the unstarted sets free to be executed under the old assumptions, which is the race this set exists to prevent.

options.option: Blocking everywhere - every spec must conform.
options.consequence: Fails 360 of 363 planned sessions and breaks 'spec_admission --all --check' in CI immediately. Retrofitting 40+ historical specs is a declared non-goal of this set and would be meaningless, since their sessions are closed and rewriting their step text changes nothing that will ever run.

options.option: Silently grandfather everything that predates the check.
options.consequence: Explicitly excluded by the source-of-record note: that is how the check ends up proving nothing. Not put to the operator.

operator_attestation: Operator ratified on 2026-08-12 at the Session 1 registration stop: 'Blocking for unstarted sets, but an information note for the rest -- don't suggest a warning. It was a different time and a different approach. Leave it at that.' The operator separately ruled the verdict be called 'require restructuring' rather than 'refuse'.
